alex: FYI - after yesterday's micro-slice experiment, we still see pcie root contention: dedicated micro-slices landed on different cards but same root path, so p50 stayed noisy. proposing three quick mitigations: (1) add `pcie_root_id` discovery + inventory tag, (2) carveout preflight that fails when cards map to same root, (3) short-lived scheduler preference `spread_root=true` for micro-slices. thoughts?

nora: agree. discovery can be lightweight: ssh+lspci, produce `pcie_root:<hex>` per GPU, push to inventory with TTL=7d. we should cache in scheduler for 10s to avoid perf hit.

diego: add CLI check: `fleetctl carveout create --check-root` that rejects placements collapsing to same root. also run `fleetctl carveout verify --probe=lspci-root` post-alloc to confirm.

infra-bot: CHANGE created: CHANGE-7342 by alex - discovery canary scheduled 2026-05-03T02:00:00Z. Ticket INV-7342.

alex: canary plan: run discovery on rack07-host[01..04], push tags, enable spread_root for carveouts only in staging, create one micro-slice for t-stream and verify metrics (pcie_stalls, preempt_count, placement_latency) for 6h. rollback flips flag off and purges tags.

nora: metrics & alerts: fail if placement_latency.p50 > baseline+200ms or if pcie_stalls doesn't drop by >=10% in 6h. I'll take pager first 3h.

diego: add low-level probe script in repo and unit tests that mock identical root ids to exercise spread algorithm.

alex: OK I'll run canary and post results here. keep it short and reversible.
